### D-ARCH-113 · 2026-11-14 · principal-architect · PR38-SEC-03 (LOW), PR38-SEC-04 (INFO), PR #38 code review R1-m1 / R2-n1, D-TASK020-41, D-SEC-PR38-02: credential headers never reach a handler (`defineRoute` refuses them in `schema.headers`, companion exception for `x-quote-token` on exactly `[session]`), one authenticator contract for TASK-052/055/091/171/261, fail-closed descriptor test, `$_terms` container shape (ADR-0008 amendment 6; api/README §8; risks R-ARCH-30)
- **Decision:** (1) `CREDENTIAL_HEADER_NAMES` in `@platform/shared` (`authorization`, `cookie`, `x-csrf-token`, `x-reauth-proof`, `x-quote-token`, `stripe-signature`, `x-mock-signature`, `x-carrier-signature`), fed to `presentedKinds` and pinned by a parity test against `openapi.yaml` `securitySchemes`; `defineRoute` refuses any of them in `schema.headers` at module load, case-insensitively, except `x-quote-token` when `route.auth` is exactly `[session]` (the ADR-0008 am. 5 companion on `claimQuote`, `saveQuote`, `createShipment`; hashes compared in constant time, never logged); `route-metadata.ts` enforces companion parity instead of a blanket `PIPELINE_HEADERS` entry. (2) Every real authenticator learns credential presence only through `presentedKinds(req.headers, route.auth)` (a signature authenticator reads its own header only on `[signature]` routes), builds permissions with `readonlySet`, calls `markCredentialsRead` together with its decision, and relies on the problem handler's descriptor-based declared test for `private, no-store` on refusals. (3) Problem handler third arm `(route === undefined || !credentialsReadOf(res)) && presentsCredential(req.headers)`. (4) `extensionProblems` refuses a non-plain `$_terms` container and reports non-plain nested objects other than `RegExp` and Joi references. Owners: (1), (3), (4) TASK-020 part 020-C, due before batch 1.3 and before TASK-055 / the first module route with `schema.headers`; (2) the five authenticator tasks.
- **Why:** the PR #38 probe delivered all three credential headers to `[anonymous]` handlers through `schema.headers`, contradicting ADR-0008 am. 5 item 1; the drift test is lane A, un-owned and bypassed by fixture routes; the five authenticators need one normative text; the companion case is already design (am. 5 table) and the contract declares it as a parameter.
- **Alternatives rejected:** a hard-coded list inside `define-route.ts` (drifts when a provider is added; the shared file is CODEOWNED and read by the slot too); refusing `x-quote-token` everywhere (would force the companion into the body or an unrelated slot); deriving signature names from the contract at run time (the api must not parse `openapi.yaml`).
- **Reversibility:** High (a list and a module-load rule).

### D-ARCH-116 · 2026-11-14 · principal-architect · PR #39 D-TASK014-02 confirmed under OI-08: api/worker runtime = digest-pinned `debian:trixie-slim` + the Node binary of the digest-pinned `node:24.22.3-trixie-slim`; rules — codename parity, binary-only copy, two-line CVE response through Dependabot `docker`/`docker-compose`, no system CA store, shell kept; distroless superseded as the OI-08 fallback (ADR-0001 amendment 2026-11-14; platform.md §3.2, §12.2 OI-03/OI-08 resolved)
- **Decision:** the `runtime` stage of `apps/{api,worker}/Dockerfile` is `debian:<codename>-slim@sha256` with exactly one artefact copied from the `node:<exact>-<codename>-slim@sha256` base, `/usr/local/bin/node`; both tags share the Debian codename (lane A rule `runtime-codename`, R3); npm, corepack, yarn, headers and `ca-certificates` stay out; Node CVEs are answered by a `node:` tag + digest bump and OS CVEs by a `debian:` digest bump, both proposed by Dependabot (`docker` for the five Dockerfiles, `docker-compose` for `compose.yaml`; 7-day cooldown; R2) and shipped by rebuild; outbound TLS uses Node's bundled CA store, the PostgreSQL CA is a file under `/etc/ssl/platform` (`/etc/ssl/certs` is absent), `--use-openssl-ca` is a fail-closed trap to remove from the allow-list (R4); `/bin/sh` and `/usr/bin/env` stay because the entrypoint preflight needs them before the first Node process.
- **Why:** measured fixed cost 204.6 MiB (Debian 83.6 + node 121.0) against a 300 MiB budget; the full node base adds ≈ 47 MiB and would put api ≈ 324 / worker ≈ 344 MiB; the official binary needs glibc ≥ 2.28 and links libstdc++/libgcc dynamically only (verified `ldd`), so the same-release pairing is safe by construction and `node --version` at build is the fail-fast; OI-08's distroless fallback removes the shell the preflight depends on and swaps the pinned official Node build for Google's.
- **Alternatives rejected:** full `node:24-trixie-slim` runtime (over budget); `gcr.io/distroless/nodejs24-debian12` (no shell, non-official Node, bookworm); `strip`ping the binary (no binutils in slim, N-API risk, unmeasured).
- **Reversibility:** Medium (one Dockerfile stage per service; the lane A rule and Dependabot entries follow).

### D-ARCH-120 · 2026-11-14 · principal-architect · PR42-SEC-01 (MEDIUM): organisation-less transactions are admitted by class — `auth` (rate classes `auth`/`email-send`), `guest:<hash>`, `public` — under one anonymous ceiling with `auth` and guest reserves; owner TASK-284 `admitcls`, a dependency of TASK-052 (ADR-0007 amendment 11 item 1; data-model §7.7; risks R-ARCH-32)
- **Decision:** the pipeline `tx` slot derives `TenantContext.admissionClass` from `route.rateLimit` and the guest token hash; ceiling `DB_ANON_MAX_CONCURRENT_TX` (default = tenant cap, ≤ it); reserves `DB_ANON_AUTH_RESERVE` (default `max(1, floor(ceiling/2))`) and `DB_ANON_GUEST_RESERVE` (1 when ceiling ≥ 4, else 0), `auth + guest ≤ ceiling − 1`; admission while `inflight(class) < ceiling − Σ others max(inflight, reserve)`; per guest key ≤ `min(2, ceiling − auth reserve)`; gauge kinds `anon_auth|anon_guest|anon_public`; worker unchanged. Verification: D3b-shape unit test (15 slow `public` loops → ≥ 95 % `auth` admitted, a second guest admitted), api test (`listCountries` flood, `createSession` non-503), route-metadata derivation test. Security-analyst adds the threat and SEC-TC text.

- **Alternatives rejected:** fixed per-class partitions (starve idle classes); per-class caps without a ceiling (anonymous share grows past one tenant); per-client sub-key for `public` (recorded lever; needs the trusted chain, useless against the distributed case); amending ADR-0006 (the mechanism is ADR-0007's).
- **Reversibility:** High (one module, three keys).

### D-ARCH-123 · 2026-11-14 · principal-architect (functional confirmation product-manager D-067) · PR43-SEC-09 (a): the invitation row is the pending state — no `INVITED` membership is written in M0/M1, acceptance inserts the membership as `ACTIVE`, the DR-A14 users positive list is `('ACTIVE','SUSPENDED')`, `INVITED` reserved (data-model §1.7, `memberships`, `invitations`, §4.3; PR #43 fix cycle changes the template; TASK-037/049/227/231 lines)
- **Decision:** as titled; 409 `ALREADY_MEMBER` checks ACTIVE or SUSPENDED members of the inviter's own organisation; pending invitations listed to `org:member:invite` holders only; a future writer of `INVITED` needs an ADR amendment.
- **Why:** `memberships.user_id NOT NULL` already made an INVITED row impossible for an address without an account; writing one at invite time would resolve e-mail → user id (account-existence oracle) and let the organisation read the invitee's profile row before consent through `p_users__org_member_read`; `invitations` already models the pending state.

- **Reversibility:** High before US-083 ships (M1 Should).

(30) The diff gate is independent of `.gitattributes` and host git config (`--text --no-textconv --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/`; `Binary files … differ` fails closed); CODEOWNERS `/.gitattributes`, `**/.gitattributes`. (32) Case and slash folding on win32 only; duplicate folded keys fail closed; repo test: no tracked paths differ only in case. ### D-ORCH-066 · 2026-11-14 · sdlc-orchestrator · PR #40 r2 APPROVED_WITH_NITS; D-TASK015-22/28 amended; R2-m1 (a) code-comment half deferred

### D-ARCH-126 · 2026-11-14 · principal-architect · Lane A is scoped by the push, with verified proof inheritance: a docs-only push runs the fast lane in light mode and inherits the head-code checks from a run on a code-identical commit; `ci-gate` verifies the proof through the jobs API; `cancel-in-progress: false` on pull requests (ADR-0023 amendment L item 1; `rulings/wave-0-ci-minutes.md` §3 (1), §4 RR-1/3/6/7)
- **Decision:** as titled. Classification by `github.event.before`→head (unknown = code); docs allow-list = one base-ref constant (am. G item 4 list ∪ `.claude/**` − `.claude/settings.json` ∪ `*.md` outside code roots); light mode skips exactly the steps already gated by `env.CODE == 'true'`; a code proof is a set of `success` step conclusions (CODE-gated required steps of `fast-lane`, gitleaks/Semgrep/openapi-breaking of `scans`) on a commit whose tree diff to the head is docs-only, read with `actions: read` from no-head-code jobs with the token on that step only; `ci-gate` is red on a light run of a code push, a docs push without a proof, or an empty output.
- **Why:** 59 of 123 PR runs this month re-ran a 6.6-minute lane on a code tree an earlier run had proved (records, evidence, quality docs); the existing docs-only classifier reads the PR range, so it never applied. The base-ref gates that decide (evidence verifier, record check, gitleaks, policy, install flags, migration immutability) still run on every exact head; only head-code checks are inherited, and only across byte-identical code trees.
- **Alternatives rejected:** skipping hosted CI on docs pushes (the evidence verifier and gitleaks must run on the exact head); trusting the job conclusion of the previous run (a light success would chain); a classifier job ahead of `fast-lane` (one more billed minute per run, F-01); keeping `cancel-in-progress: true` (a cancelled full run leaves the docs push unprovable).
- **Reversibility:** High (one classifier, step conditions already in place, one concurrency flag).

### D-ARCH-127 · 2026-11-14 · principal-architect · `security-integration` runs once per code tree, on merge-candidate heads (security record `pass`/`not-required`), with proof inheritance; `package-lock.json` selects it only for production-closure changes (ADR-0023 amendment L item 2; ruling §3 (2)–(3), §4 RR-2/4/5)
- **Decision:** as titled; otherwise the job is skipped and `ci-gate` is red with `security-integration pending`; never dropped to save minutes; degraded mode still excludes these paths.
- **Why:** 33 of 45 PRs select the job (plan: 15), every push ran it (≈ 190 runs a month), and the six suites will cost ≈ 8 min a run (≈ 1,500 min, most of the allowance). The record push is the merge candidate in practice (almost every green run this month); the independent Linux proof per PR is kept, at ≈ 62 runs a month. Dev-only dependency bumps change nothing the suites prove.
- **Alternatives rejected:** folding into lane B (loses the independent pre-merge Linux run SEC-P3-07 asked for); a `ready` label or dispatch (manual, and no cheaper than the record signal); path→suite selection as the first lever (≈ 1–2 min of 8; deferred).
- **Reversibility:** High.

### D-ORCH-090 · 2026-11-15 · sdlc-orchestrator · PR #46 r2 code CHANGES_REQUESTED; proof binding fixed in-PR; no-retarget rule
- **Decision:** PR #46 code r2 at ad30316 = CHANGES_REQUESTED (round-1 items all fixed; 88/98 mutants killed). **R2-M1 (MAJOR)** = PR46-SEC-13 widened: `lookupProofs` accepts any completed `pull_request` run on a code-identical commit from any PR and never checks its base, and `ci.yml` has no `branches:` filter, so a run against another base branch (whose workflow and base-ref tools come from that base) can be adopted as the code/security proof; the retarget-for-one-push variant also defeats "ci-gate green on the exact SHA". **Ruling:** fix in this PR (not a residual): (1) accept proofs only from runs of this PR's head branch whose run lists exactly this PR, with base `main`, and no `base_ref_changed` since; (2) `on.pull_request.branches: [main]` with a base-ref policy pin; (3) treat an empty/ambiguous `pull_requests` field as "no proof". **Rule (no-retarget):** agents never change a PR's base branch; any retarget makes all prior proofs and records void and requires a full run. R2-m1 (ci-gate's own-run step reading untested) and R2-n1 pins ride the same cycle. **R2-m2** (`devOptional` packages such as the Prisma CLI treated as dev in the lockfile rule) → principal-architect amends ADR-0023 am. ### D-TASK020-78..94 · 2026-11-15 · senior-developer (logged by orchestrator per D-ORCH-040) · PR #54 (020-D) decisions
- **D-TASK020-78: `rawSystemTable` reads identifiers only, as ruled.** String-literal and comment contents are not names (fold 7 §(9)). Residual, stated in the rule header and pinned in the corpus: SQL text inside a string that a function executes (`query_to_xml('select … from t', …)`) or concatenates. `DO` is refused by `db-raw-sql`; such functions are a review item. One finding per table per template. The partition rule is generalised to `<any SYSTEM table>_YYYY_MM` (ruling names `audit_entries`); index-like names such as `audit_entries__x` or `audit_entries_count` do not match. The manifests are read for every raw template and missing manifests fail closed, so fixture roots that contain raw templates carry a miniature manifest (`db-raw-sql`, and after the PR #42 union the T-83 root).
- **D-TASK020-79: `audit` owner entry lists both globs.** An explicit owner entry replaces the module default, so `apps/*/src/modules/audit/**` is listed beside `packages/audit/src/**`; `data_subjects` (audit manifest) is owned the same way. PR #42's store (`packages/audit/src/store/prisma-store.ts`) lints clean.
- **D-TASK020-80: raw-statement forms.** First keyword of every statement (comments and literals skipped), plus two anywhere-forms (the setting function without a literal `true` is_local; `UPDATE` with `pg_settings`). `PREPARE` covers both `PREPARE TRANSACTION` and a named prepared statement (session state); `EXECUTE`/`DEALLOCATE` are session forms. `SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY` is admitted only through an exact-file option (`allow: ['read-only-transaction']`) on `apps/api/src/platform/db/with-tenant-tx.ts`; `SET TRANSACTION READ WRITE` there is still reported. The TenantDb guard has no allowance (withTenantTx sends that statement on the raw transaction client, not through the guard). The literal-`true` rule keeps PR #42's transaction-local `lock_timeout` statement working (it is a corpus case and the store suites run in lane B).
- **D-TASK020-81: two twins, one corpus.** The api may not import tools and tools may not import the api, so the lexer exists twice (`tools/eslint-rules/raw-sql-lexer.mjs`, `apps/api/src/platform/db/raw-statement.ts`) and both test suites run `tests/fixtures/sql/raw-statement-corpus.json` (67 cases + 5 allowance cases, residuals marked). The corpus is JSON so it may spell the setter and Unicode-escape forms that `platform/tenant-context-sql` refuses in source. Name and keyword comparisons in both twins are regular-expression literals for the same reason. Residuals (allowed by both, pinned): a function or procedure body that commits or sets (bootstrap/migration DDL lane; runtime roles cannot create functions), `CALL` (a procedure cannot COMMIT inside a transaction block), SQL text in a string.
- **D-TASK020-82: `TenantDbAccessError` for a refused statement**, message `<member> with a <form> statement (<keyword>)`; never the statement text or values (they are bound and never reach it). A 500 programming error like the other guard refusals.

That is stricter than ADR-0005 am. 11 item 22 (d) ("one same-function const alias"); it closes R2-m3 failing closed and the R2-n3 factory shape. Destructured holder methods (`const { add } = deps.queue; add()`) are reported too. principal-architect may record it as an amendment note; no code depends on the narrower reading.

### D-TASK029-01..15 · 2026-11-16 · senior-developer (recorded by orchestrator) · TASK-029 automatic audit capture (PR #56)
- **01** Capture lives in `apps/api/src/platform/audit/capture.ts` (`createAuditCapture` → `mount`/`denied`), not the sheet's `audit-middleware.ts`; the tx slot is its only value importer; pipeline.ts gets the factory via a re-export from `execute.ts`.
- **02** `auditEntityId` on `defineRoute` is optional. Default: CREATE → result `id`; a `:<entity>Id` path parameter; none for a list VIEW. Anything else fails to mount, naming method and path.
- **03** Write actions: `record` + the transaction's one `flush`, as the last work in the handler tx. VIEW/DOWNLOAD: their own short tx after COMMIT and before send; SENSITIVE fails closed (503 `AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE`, Retry-After 1); NORMAL is best effort.
- **04** A *returned* 409/422/5xx commits a FAILED entry in the handler tx; other returned 4xx write no entry.
- **05** LOGIN, LOGOUT, MFA_ENROLLED and STATE_TRANSITION are refused at mount until their domain recorder exists.
- **06** PERMISSION_DENIED is written in its own tx before the 403; a failed write answers 500/503, never a silent 403; no entity id; 401s are not audited.
- **07** Client-shaped columns are kept only in the writer's shape, otherwise null (PR42-SEC-15 a/b); NUL and lone surrogates → 400 at the JSON boundary (SEC-15 c).
- **08** STREAM_MISMATCH: a tenant entry must match the tx org; an org-less tx accepts only the SYSTEM shard; I3 via the `beforeCommit` port; one writer per process.
- **09** PR42-SEC-17 uses H2 (statement tracking + `setImmediate` settle loop); timer-started writes are a documented residual, backstopped by TASK-033.
- **10** PR42-SEC-19: `write`/`flush` return already-handled promises.
- **11** `AUDIT_NONE_ROUTES` is pinned both ways against the contract's NONE operations.
- **12** The list filter summary has sorted keys, all values tokenised as PERSONAL; `result_count` comes from the `data` array, otherwise null.
- **13** `source_app` = `X-Client-App` when web|admin, otherwise `api`.
- **14** FAILED entries also cover `load`/`call` phase failures (REQ-AUDIT-010); none when the audit path or the admission bulkhead itself failed.
- **15** The branch keeps its dispatched name (`…-automatic-audit-capture`), not the sheet's.
- **Follow-up (MEDIUM, latent) → TASK-028:** production `startApi` composition has no tokeniser/ipIndex/UA parser, so any audited route or PERMISSION_DENIED in a deployed process fails closed with 500 `TOKENISER_UNAVAILABLE`. Wire them through `AppDependencies` into `createAuditCapture` before the first audited module route; the UA parser owner to be confirmed by TASK-028. Other follow-ups: TASK-031 (old/new diffs, reason), TASK-030 (per-stream CTE), TASK-033 (T0 residual backstop), TASK-047 (SEC-17/19 on the job port), qa-lead (activate the audit-generator suite; move SEC-TC-74 to required_cases).
- **Reversibility:** High.

### D-TASK029-16 · 2026-11-17 · sdlc-orchestrator · Supersedes D-TASK029-04 (PR #56 code R1-M1 = PR56-SEC-09)
- **Decision:** any status ≥ 400 that a handler *returns* rolls back the handler transaction; 409/422/5xx write the FAILED entry in its own transaction (ADR-0007 §Capture and REQ-AUDIT-010 as written); returned 400/403/404 commit nothing and write nothing.
- **Why:** the old rule committed handler writes with no entry, or under a FAILED entry an auditor reads as "nothing changed", and re-executed on retry after a returned 5xx (ADR-0014). Following the existing ADR needs no architect ruling.
- **Alternatives rejected:** an architect ruling accepting the commit (contradicts O4 audit completeness).
- **Reversibility:** High.

### D-TASK029-17..24 · 2026-11-17 · senior-developer (recorded by orchestrator) · PR #56 fix cycle 1 (@9746b2f, code f750cc4)
- **17** D-TASK029-16 is implemented through `RouteReturnedError` (in `define-route.ts`), thrown inside the handler tx for a returned status ≥ 400. FAILED details are `{status}` only. A returned 5xx leaves no idempotency completion, so a retry re-executes (ADR-0014). **→ TASK-040:** store the 4xx idempotency completion outside the rolled-back handler tx.
- **18** SEC-01 is fixed by sanitising the filter summary, not by refusing at the boundary: empty or NUL values are stored JSON-encoded; `MAX_FILTER_TEXT` = 1,024 code points with an ellipsis. A NORMAL list is never served without its entry for a client-chosen value.
- **19** Routes with `x-audit.additional[]` (`createQuoteShare`, `checkoutOrder`) are refused at mount until a recording seam exists.
- **20** SEC-02: `pipeline.ts` is the single capture composition point (exact-file lint category `api-pipeline-composition`); the R3-n2 scan covers `platform/tx/**` and `pipeline.ts`.
- **21** A tokeniser is required at mount for audited routes and for routes that can answer 403 (both errors name TASK-028); a missing UA parser or IP index leaves `ua_parsed`/`ip_hash` null.
- **22** No FAILED write after TRANSACTION_UNAVAILABLE, STATEMENT_TIMEOUT or LOCK_TIMEOUT, or when the client went away; the response waits at most 1 s (`FAILED_ENTRY_WAIT_MS`) for the FAILED write.
- **23** VIEW/DOWNLOAD handler txs are read-only.
- **24** Capture log events `audit.view_unrecorded`, `audit.failed_unrecorded` and `audit.entity_id_unresolved`, with class-only fields (no values).
- **Not taken:** NITs R1-n2 (head-row stamp, metadata only) and R1-n3 (a `setImmediate` turn before COMMIT → note for the TASK-030 performance budget).
- **Reversibility:** High.

### D-ARCH-142 · 2026-11-17 · principal-architect · T-39 / PR56-SEC-03: per-actor denial budget on TASK-041 — N individual `PERMISSION_DENIED` entries a minute (default 20), one aggregated entry at the crossing, then 429 `RATE_LIMITED` without a write; the suppressed count is carried into the first entry of a later window; in-memory fallback on a Valkey outage
- **Decision:** as titled. Key = organisation (or `system`) and actor; the budget is taken in the authorise slot before `capture.denied` (TASK-041 takes `api-authz` and `api-routing`); D-TASK029-06 is unchanged. Due before the first route with a catalogued permission: TASK-049 already depends on TASK-041, and the orchestrator does not back-fill a permission-gated route task ahead of it.
- **Why:** authorisation runs before the route limiter, so every denial costs a tenant transaction, vault statements and the stream-head lock; the budget bounds that to N+1 audit transactions a minute per actor. An entry that closes the window has no request to write it, and a job would need the worker audit port (TASK-047, later), so the aggregated entry is written at the crossing and the count follows lazily.
- **Alternatives rejected:** moving the denial write after the route limiter (it counts by class and user, not by denial); a scheduled job that closes windows; unlimited denials with a longer lock timeout.
- **Reversibility:** High. Security-analyst confirms the aggregated-entry shape against PR56-SEC-03; qa-lead the SEC-TC-15 wording.

### D-ARCH-148 · 2026-11-17 · principal-architect · PR #61 R1-m3 (a) / PR61-SEC-07 / D-TASK028-03: the vault token columns `audit_entries.ip_token`, `user_agent_token` and `reason_token` are INTERNAL — the code is right; data-model §3.4 amended from "PER (token)" to "INT (token)"
- **Decision:** as titled. "PER (token)" was a note on what the token stands for, not a registry class. A vault token, in a `*_token` column or as `{"$pii": …}` inside `old_value`, `new_value` and `details`, is an opaque UUIDv7 reference. The PERSONAL value exists in `audit_pii_vault` only, and the token resolves only through the vault under `audit:read`. Catalog C10 keeps its wording and gets no exception for `audit_entries`.
- **Code (PR #61 fix cycle 1):** a comment only. The header of `packages/shared/src/classification/registry.ts` cites D-ARCH-148 and data-model §3.4 as amended.
- **Why:** ADR-0007 rests on "the chain hashes the token, never the value" and "archived partitions contain no personal data"; a PERSONAL class would contradict both and would ask the redaction to tokenise a token. §3.4 already classes the JSON columns that carry the same tokens `INT (tokenised)`, and C10 lists no exception for `audit_entries`.
- **Alternatives rejected:** PERSONAL plus three C10 exceptions (the exception list would then cover the table the SYSTEM rule exists for); a sixth class `TOKEN` (REQ-AUDIT-009 has five, and no handling would differ from INTERNAL).
- **Reversibility:** High.

### D-ARCH-149 · 2026-11-17 · principal-architect · PR61-SEC-03 / PR #61 R1-m3 (b) — D-TASK028-04 amended: filter values of an authenticated list request belong to the actor's data subject; a value without a known person belongs to the unattributed subject of its UTC month, not to one permanent ANONYMOUS subject; each month is erased 12 months after it ends by the EPIC-B-413 retention job; two code changes in the PR #61 fix cycle
- **Decision:** as titled (ADR-0007 amendment 13 items 4–6; data-model §1.6, §3.4 `data_subjects`, §5.7, §10.5).
- **Code (PR #61 fix cycle 1), exactly two changes:**
  1. `apps/api/src/platform/audit/descriptor-runtime.ts`: `filterSummary(query, subject)`, called with `principal.authenticated ? { kind: 'USER', refId: principal.actorId } : null`. Unit: `entryFor` on an authenticated list request yields filter values owned by the actor; on an anonymous one, `subject: null`. The fix cycle holds `api-audit-mw` for this file (free: TASK-052 and TASK-060 are not in flight).
  2. `packages/audit/src/redaction/vault.ts`: the constant `UNATTRIBUTED_SUBJECT` becomes `unattributedSubject(at)` = `{ kind: 'USER', refId }`, where `refId` is the ANONYMOUS actor id with its first 12 hex digits set to `Date.UTC(year, month, 1)` in hex, zero-padded (November 2026: `01a19467-e800-7000-8000-000000000002`). `VaultTokeniserOptions.now` (default `Date.now`) is read once per `tokenise` call, and the export in `index.ts` follows. Unit: the November id above, a different id for December, one subject for two values of one call, a value that names its subject unchanged. No DDL and no migration. At a month's first instants, concurrent writers wait on one `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` insert for the length of one transaction, as for any new subject today; the insert-order item of the fix-cycle triage (session B R1-m5), if taken, covers this subject too.
- **Retention:** kept in this run (no retention job; `platform_erasure` is unused; synthetic data only). For production, the subject of month M is erased with the existing erase-by-subject statement once M ended 12 months ago, and the viewer shows `[ERASED]`. The period is a proposed default; product-manager confirms it with the retention schedule.
- **Owners:**
  - items 1–2: TASK-028;
  - the retention job, "no revival" (the tokeniser stores nothing for a subject whose `erased_at` is set) and erasure by value (`value_hmac` does not depend on the subject): EPIC-B-413 Privacy workflows (M4), a G4 precondition for a production release; no Run-1 task;
  - `API_KEY` actors: EPIC-B-303 (M3) — the key's owning user, otherwise the month subject;
  - PR61-SEC-08: destroying the retired `AUDIT_INDEX_KEY` version (ADR-0018: 90 days after the yearly rotation) is a step of the M5 rotation runbook and bounds `ip_hash` enumeration at about 15 months.
- **Why:** the vault's unique key `(subject_id, entity_name, field, value_hmac)` reuses a token for a repeated value. Under one permanent subject the age of a row is the first sighting of the value, so an age-based delete would erase an address used yesterday, or need a scan of every entry. A subject per month makes retention the existing statement. A search term is the searcher's activity, and over-erasing a third party's name is the safe direction.
- **Alternatives rejected:** one ANONYMOUS subject plus a job that finds unreferenced tokens (they sit in two unindexed columns and inside `details`); a new `data_subjects.kind` (bootstrap-lane DDL and a late task, for a label); no raw IP or user agent for anonymous actors (failed sign-ins lose the exact address); attributing filter values to the person searched for (unknown at capture).
- **Reversibility:** High until production data exists; the reserved ids are load-bearing after that.

### D-ARCH-151 · 2026-11-18 · principal-architect · Operator organisation: a reserved row of the TASK-037 migration, inserted before FORCE (D-ORCH-COORD-03 item 1; ADR-0005 amendment 12)
- **Decision:**
  - The migration that creates `organisations` inserts the one OPERATOR organisation next to the reserved users: id `00000000-0000-7000-8000-000000000010` (constant `OPERATOR_ORG_ID`), `display_name` `Operator`, the SYSTEM actor in `created_by` and `updated_by`, `ON CONFLICT ("id") DO NOTHING`. It comes after `ux_organisations__single_operator` and before `ENABLE` + `FORCE`. The header stays `data-changing: no`.
  - No seed, job or operator step creates the organisation. The reference seed writes GLOBAL tables only. The demo seed (TASK-089) adds staff memberships to the reserved organisation and never creates or renames it. `seedId('org:operator')` is withdrawn.
  - AT-US-061-01 stays on TASK-037. D-TASK037-04 (re-route to TASK-089) is superseded. D-TASK037-03 (reserved users in the migration) is confirmed.
  - No fixture plants an OPERATOR organisation any more; a fixture adds a membership to `OPERATOR_ORG_ID`.
- **Why:**
  - After `FORCE` the migrator has no policy on `organisations`, and the demo seed never runs with `APP_ENV=production`. As designed, production had no operator organisation at all.
  - `p_organisations__active` checks only `id = platform.app_org_id()`, and the creating service chooses that value. On an empty index the service rule was the only control against a `platform_app` session creating the first OPERATOR organisation and a membership in it. The reserved row occupies the unique index in every migrated database.
  - It needs no new role, policy, definer write or credential.
- **Alternatives rejected:**
  - A privileged job after `migrate`: it needs the break-glass credential for routine work, a write-capable definer function, or a policy for the migrator (against ADR-0005 amendment 6 and ADR-0007 amendment 7).
  - The demo seed or an admin flow as `platform_app`: it never runs in production, leaves the slot open until it runs, and needs one service path that creates OPERATOR, which REQ-ORG-001 excludes.
  - A production command that creates the organisation with the first staff user: the same objections, plus an operational step that can be forgotten.
- **Functional acceptance criteria:** unchanged, so product-manager was not brought in. The Then-clause of AT-US-061-01 holds as written. Wording for the next story edit: REQ-ORG-001 "(created by seed)" and the scenario title.
- **Not verified here:** no test was run (host rule of D-ORCH-131). What PostgreSQL refuses is read from the policy and migration text of PR #65 at `d3c2c16`.
- **Where:** ADR-0005 amendment 12 items 23 to 25; data-model §1.6, §3.2, §4.3, §8.3 rule 10, §9.1 to §9.3, A30; `docs/03-architecture/rulings/wave-1-batch-1.1-rulings.md` §2 (exact statement and the per-task list); cards TASK-037 and TASK-089.
- **Reversibility:** High until PR #65 merges (one statement in an unmerged migration). After that the row is permanent: a later migration can neither add nor remove it, because the migrator cannot write the table.

### D-ARCH-152 · 2026-11-18 · principal-architect · `createOrganisation`: the contract adds an optional `type`; the acceptance criteria stand (D-ORCH-COORD-03 item 2)
- **Decision:**
  - `OrganisationCreateRequest` gains the optional property `type`: the four organisation types, default `BUSINESS_CUSTOMER`. `OrganisationPatch` stays without it (400 `UNKNOWN_FIELD`, AT-US-061-03).
  - Every value but `BUSINESS_CUSTOMER` is refused by the service with 422 `ORG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED` and audited with outcome `FAILED`. A value outside the enumeration is 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`.
  - The edit lands in the TASK-224 PR with the route, the Joi schema, the tests and the regenerated types (api/README §18 item 1). The exact YAML is in the rulings file §3.3 and is the approved change request.
  - PR #65 needs no contract change. Its service already takes `type` and refuses everything but `BUSINESS_CUSTOMER`.
- **Why:**
  - The contract already describes `ORG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED` on `createOrganisation` and lists it on that operation only. A closed schema without `type` makes the code unreachable, so the schema is the defect.
  - REQ-AUDIT-010 writes no audit entry for a 400. With the closed schema AT-US-061-05 (a `FAILED` entry for the refused attempt) fails as well as AT-US-061-02.
  - One schema property changes, against three requirement artefacts on the other side.
  - D-ARCH-151 makes it safe below the service: the database refuses OPERATOR (occupied unique index), INDIVIDUAL (`ck_organisations__personal_owner`) and PARTNER (the owner role link fails the role-scope trigger in the same transaction).
- **Why not on `main` now:** `openapi.yaml` is a tooling input. A change makes the lane-B evidence of every open PR stale, and `types.gen.ts` must be regenerated in the same commit, which is product code. No route mounts the operation before TASK-224.
- **Alternatives rejected:**
  - Amend the criteria to 400 `UNKNOWN_FIELD`: REQ-ORG-001, AT-US-061-02 and AT-US-061-05 change, the refused attempt is no longer audited, and `ORG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED` becomes unreachable through the API.
  - An enumeration with `BUSINESS_CUSTOMER` only: PARTNER would fail validation and be a 400 again.
  - A contract-only PR now: stale evidence and CI minutes for an operation nothing mounts.
- **Specialists:** api-designer and product-manager were not dispatched. The change is one property and one example, and no acceptance criterion changes.
- **Open, not decided here (orchestrator to product-manager):** US-061 and US-062 are M0 Must and demo-critical, but their route-level scenarios now close in TASK-224 and TASK-231 (Wave 8, Should, cuttable). The cards still say TASK-037 completes both stories. Recommended default: record both as partial on TASK-037 and completed by TASK-224 and TASK-231, which makes those routes non-cuttable. Alternative: move the route-level scenarios to US-082 and US-085.
- **Not verified here:** the YAML was not linted (host rule). TASK-224 runs `openapi:lint` and `openapi:types`.
- **Where:** rulings file §3 and §4; cards TASK-224 (change request and the US-061 scenarios), TASK-037, TASK-231 (the US-062 scenarios of D-ORCH-131).
- **Reversibility:** High until TASK-224 merges. After that, removing the property is a breaking contract change.

### D-SEC-PR64-01 · 2026-11-18 · security-analyst · PR #64 (TASK-035) security r1 = PASS_WITH_CONDITIONS at `90ef83f` (record `docs/05-quality/security/PR-0064-TASK-035-security-review.md`, committed on main)
- **Decision:** 0 Critical/High; 2 MEDIUM, 4 LOW, 5 INFO. Static review plus light Node probes (host rule of D-ORCH-131; no install, Jest, Docker or worktree commands). Lane B has not run; this round does not replace it.
  - **Sound:** tenant context is never read from the payload (closed Joi schema at both levels, `convert: false`; `org_id`/`actor_id` refused and flagged `job_context_mismatch`; processors get the validated clone; the job name selects nothing); the producer writes identifiers only and never generates a correlation id; the api ACL user has no `~bull:*`; the dead-letter record is deep-redacted and bounded; connection options come from `buildValkeyOptions` (pinned TLS, no URL); retries bounded and clamped; kindless queues fail closed.
  - **Dependency:** `joi` ^18.3.2 in `@platform/shared` adds no package (already locked for api and config); BSD-3-Clause; past every joi and @hapi/hoek advisory; maintained. Off the browser-safe barrel.
  - **D-TASK035-01..06:** no security objection (06 observed under PR64-SEC-08).
- **PR64-SEC-01 (MEDIUM, CWE-532) = merge condition C1:** the 18 BullMQ `Queue` instances in `runtime.ts` (and the consumer-owned DLQ queue) have no `error` listener; on an AUTH refusal BullMQ `console.error`s the ioredis error, whose `command.args` carry `HELLO 3 AUTH worker <password>`. Probe: 97 cleartext copies on stderr in 3 s, 0 log lines; with a listener, 0. Fix: one `openQueue` factory that always attaches a class-only listener, a fake-RESP-server test and a source-scan test → **this PR**, then a security delta round. The fix touches only unowned files, so ci-gate stays green on this record: the orchestrator holds the merge until the delta round (sim S6).
- **PR64-SEC-02 (MEDIUM, CWE-359, T-74):** BullMQ keeps raw `failedReason`, `stacktrace` and job `data` of failed jobs forever (`removeOnFail: false`), next to the redacted dead-letter copy; AT-US-009-04's sentinel stays in the failed set. Fix: rethrow a sanitised reason-only error, `job.updateData` the redacted data on PAYLOAD_INVALID, `stackTraceLimit: 0` → this PR's fix cycle, at the latest before TASK-039 registers a processor.

### D-PM-068 · 2026-11-18 · product-manager · US-061 and US-062 delivery split (D-061 form): partial on TASK-037, completed by TASK-224 and TASK-231, which are no longer cuttable; both stories are partial at `v0.1.0-m0` and complete before G3
- **Numbering:** `D-PM-` continues the product-manager series (D-008 to D-067), at the orchestrator's request. The next entry is D-PM-072.
- **Input:** the orchestrator applied the architect's recommended default of `docs/03-architecture/rulings/wave-1-batch-1.1-rulings.md` §4 (first open item; D-ARCH-152 "Open, not decided here"; D-ORCH-131 routing item 3). This entry records it and decides what it leaves open: the release each part belongs to, the tasks that become uncuttable by dependency, and the fallback.
- **Decision:**
  - **Scenario ownership, US-061 (M0 Must, DC, 5 scenarios).** TASK-037: AT-US-061-01, the service and database halves of AT-US-061-02, the database half of AT-US-061-03. TASK-224: the response halves of AT-US-061-02 (422 `ORG_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`, no row) and AT-US-061-03 (400 `UNKNOWN_FIELD`), AT-US-061-04, AT-US-061-05. TASK-224 completes the story.
  - **Scenario ownership, US-062 (M0 Must, DC, 6 scenarios).** TASK-037: AT-US-062-01 to -04, and the change record that AT-US-062-06 asserts (old/new status and role-set diff; the `[AT-US-062-06]` unit test already in PR #65). TASK-231: AT-US-062-05 and AT-US-062-06 through the member routes. TASK-231 completes the story.
  - **One clause added to the orchestrator's split: TASK-049 owns the creation clause of AT-US-062-06 at registration.** Registration is the one membership write R0 can perform. TASK-049 asserts one `membership` audit entry (new status ACTIVE, role set Owner) in the registration transaction, next to the user and organisation entries US-015 already asserts. TASK-049 depends on the unmerged TASK-037 and has no row in STATUS.md, so its card can take the line. The orchestrator may strike this clause; the R0 statement in PRD §7 then needs "except the audit entry of the registration membership".
  - **Not cuttable.** TASK-224 and TASK-231 leave ladder rung 2. TASK-227 leaves it too for as long as TASK-231 depends on it (`members` → `invite`). TASK-235 (team screens, US-268 and US-269) stays cuttable.
  - **Story tags unchanged.** US-061 and US-062 stay M0 Must DC. US-081 to US-085 stay M1 Should. What is protected is the six Must scenarios and the routes they run on: a Should scenario of US-081 to US-085 that blocks one of these tasks may still be deferred scenario by scenario, while the routes ship.
  - **R0 (`v0.1.0-m0`).** Not blocked. The tag is cut with US-061 and US-062 recorded as partial in the dossier, naming the six scenarios. The other 111 M0 Must stories are complete at R0.
  - **R1 / G3.** TASK-224 and TASK-231 are merged before the G3 evidence run. Default placement: with the Must band, before the Wave 7 exit. G3 accepts the two stories only with all eleven scenarios passing in `ac-trace.json`.
  - **Fallback, agreed now.** If TASK-224 or TASK-231 is unmerged at the Wave 7 exit, product-manager applies rung 4: the six route-level scenarios move to US-082 and US-085 as appended scenarios, US-061 and US-062 keep what TASK-037 proves, and the tasks return to rung 2. That is the architect's named alternative. It gets its own entry if used.
  - **No acceptance criterion changed.** No Gherkin line, scenario title, REQ, priority, milestone, DC tag or count changed (434 / 91 / 293 / DC 134).
- **Why:**
  - **The split is real, not a relabel.** Four US-061 scenarios need `createOrganisation` and `updateOrganisation`; two US-062 scenarios need the member routes. No M0 task mounts them. A card that says "TASK-037 completes US-061 and US-062" would let both stories read as Implemented with six scenarios unowned, which is the silent drop of D-061 and D-062.
  - **Why not in R0.** TASK-231 depends on TASK-187 (Wave 7, the step-up of REQ-AUTH-025) and on TASK-227, which depends on TASK-169 (Wave 6). Pulling them into Waves 0 to 3 would move invitations, member management and step-up onto the M0 critical path. `createOrganisation` is `x-milestone: M1`. PRD §6.1 exercises none of the six scenarios, and R0 has no route on which a refused create, a type change or a role assignment could be attempted, so nothing R0 does is unproven. R0 has no gate.
  - **Why before G3.** G3 judges Must stories, and both are Must. A refused `PARTNER` or `OPERATOR` create is a privilege probe that must be audited (D-ARCH-152), and it becomes reachable the moment the route exists.
  - **Why TASK-227 follows.** AT-US-085-05 (inviting into an INDIVIDUAL organisation) needs the invite route, and member management without a way to add members is not a usable increment. Keeping the dependency costs one M task; removing it would split a Should story across two tasks for no user value.

- **Alternatives:**
  - Move the route-level scenarios to US-082 and US-085 now (the architect's alternative). Not chosen by the orchestrator: it takes the privilege-probe audit out of the Must set. Kept as the fallback, because it costs no schedule.
  - Keep "TASK-037 completes both stories" and rely on card notes. Rejected: traceability and the gate read the completes column.
  - Pull TASK-224, TASK-227 and TASK-231 into M0. Rejected: it puts M1 step-up and invitations on the R0 critical path for scenarios the M0 demo never runs.
  - Mount a minimal create route in M0 only to prove the refusals. Rejected: a route whose only job is to refuse adds attack surface and a contract change to R0 for no user.
  - Drop the `members` → `invite` dependency so TASK-227 stays cuttable. Rejected as the default (see Why); senior-developer may still propose it.
- **Applied in:** `docs/01-requirements/stories/EPIC-03-organisations-rbac-tenancy.md` (notes of US-061, US-062, US-082, US-085; no Gherkin change), `docs/sdlc/traceability.md` 1.7 (REQ-ORG-001, -003, -004 rows; REQ-ORG-002 unchanged), `docs/01-requirements/PRD.md` 1.12 (§7, §7.1, §11), `docs/01-requirements/ASSUMPTIONS.md` A-109.

The wave rule allows an M0 Must DC story to complete in Waves 0 to 2 only, so US-061 and US-062 completing later is an error; it needs a recorded exception for these two stories that cites this entry. `cuttable` is `wave >= 8`, so the three tasks either move into Wave 7 after TASK-187 (preferred: Wave 7 exit is the G3-ready checkpoint) or carry an explicit override. `dc` is derived from the stories, so TASK-224 and TASK-231 would print "demo-critical"; they are not, the demo-critical part is TASK-037's.

### D-PM-069 · 2026-11-18 · product-manager · REQ-ORG-001 wording: the operator organisation is a reserved row of the organisations migration, not a seeded row (D-ARCH-151)
- **Decision:**
  - REQ-ORG-001 "(created by seed)" becomes "(a reserved row of the schema migration that creates the `organisations` table, present in every migrated database before any seed runs)".
  - Its note records: no seed, job, operator step, API or runtime role creates the organisation; the seeds neither create nor rename it; "operator" is decided by `type`, never by the reserved identifier; `createOrganisation` takes an optional `type` so a refused type is a 422 that is audited (D-ARCH-152); the organisation has no member until staff are provisioned (US-B-001 for production).

- **Why:**
  - After `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` the migrator has no policy on `organisations`, so the reference seed cannot write the row, and the demo seed never runs in production. Read literally, the old wording left production without an operator organisation.
  - The Then-clause of AT-US-061-01 holds as written: exactly one `OPERATOR` organisation, and an identical row count after the second seed run.
  - The scenario title is the key of AT-US-061-01 in `gherkin-test-map.md`, which the TASK-277 drift test compares with the story file. A title edit without a regenerated map turns that test red on `main` (the D-063 and D-064 convention: titles stay).

  - Leave REQ-ORG-001 and explain only in the story. Rejected: the requirement must be testable without the story, and "created by seed" is false.
- **Applied in:** `docs/01-requirements/REQUIREMENTS.md` (REQ-ORG-001 row, version line), the US-061 notes, PRD 1.12 §11.

### D-PM-070 · 2026-11-18 · product-manager · Backlog story US-B-001 for the first production staff user (`ops:staff-bootstrap`, D-ARCH-153, R-ARCH-33): M5, new epic EPIC-B-508, a G4 precondition for a production release
- **Decision:**
  - New M5 backlog epic **EPIC-B-508 Go-live bootstrap: first operator staff user**, and the story **US-B-001** with Gherkin acceptance criteria, in `docs/01-requirements/BACKLOG.md` 1.1. It is Won't (this run); at M5 it is Must and a precondition of G4 for a production release.
  - The EPIC-B-207 row says that every later staff user is created there by an existing Super Admin and points to EPIC-B-508 for the first one.
  - `US-B-NNN` is a new ID form for backlog stories written ahead of their milestone. They are outside the `US-NNN` series, the story counts, the Gherkin map and the plan generator, which read `stories/EPIC-*.md` only.
  - The story takes the architecture as fixed (runtime role, `SYSTEM_JOB` actor, pipeline task, no `OPERATOR` organisation created, refusal once a member exists) and adds product defaults, logged as A-110: refusal on a membership in any status; an existing account with a password is never promoted; an operator e-mail domain allow-list; a pipeline run reference in the audit entries; a `FAILED` audit entry for a refused run; a personal organisation for the user per DR-A06.
- **Why:**
  - **M5, not EPIC-B-207 (M2).** The command is needed only where the demo seed cannot run, which is production, and a production target exists only from M5. EPIC-B-207 is the screen set an already signed-in Super Admin uses; it cannot create the first one. Filed under M2, the story would be planned a milestone before anything can exercise it and could be closed without a production rehearsal.
  - **Its own epic.** None of EPIC-B-501 to -507 owns a one-shot identity command, and a G4 precondition is easier to track as a named row than as a line inside the delivery-pipeline epic.
  - **Written now.** D-ARCH-151 creates the gap in this run. A story with acceptance criteria keeps R-ARCH-33 from depending on someone rereading a rulings file at M5.
  - **The added defaults close two abuse paths the risk row does not name:** promoting an address an attacker registered first (the D-050 class), and re-running the command after staff were removed.
- **Alternatives:**
  - EPIC-B-207. Rejected (see Why).
  - EPIC-B-502 (progressive delivery), because the command is a pipeline task. Rejected: the behaviour is identity and tenancy, the pipeline is only the runner.
  - A Run 1 story. Rejected by D-ARCH-153: there is no production target, and staging uses the demo seed.
  - A one-line backlog row without acceptance criteria. Rejected: the orchestrator asked for Gherkin, and the refusal rules are the substance.
- **Open for M5 planning (defaults applied, A-110):** principal-architect confirms the personal-organisation reading of "creates no organisation"; security-analyst reviews the existing-account and allow-list rules; devops-engineer owns the pipeline task and its environment approval; the wrong-address recovery goes to the EPIC-B-507 break-glass runbook.
- **Applied in:** `docs/01-requirements/BACKLOG.md` 1.1, `docs/01-requirements/ASSUMPTIONS.md` A-110, the REQ-ORG-001 note, PRD 1.12 §11.
- **Reversibility:** High (backlog text; nothing is built).

### D-SEC-PR66-01 · 2026-11-18 · security-analyst · PR #66 (TASK-290) security r1 = PASS_WITH_FOLLOW-UPS at `9a14659` (record `docs/05-quality/security/PR-0066-TASK-290-security-review.md`, committed on main)
- **Decision:** 0 Critical, High or Medium; 1 LOW, 1 INFO. Static review plus light Node probes (host rule of D-ORCH-131): no npm, Jest, Docker or worktree commands. PostgreSQL facts come from `REL_18_STABLE` `scan.l` and `gram.y`, read but not executed.
  - **Sound:**
    - The block layer of `splitStatements` matches `gram.y` exactly (`opt_routine_body`, `routine_body_stmt_list`, `toplevel_stmt`). It opens on `BEGIN ATOMIC` in a routine head at depth 0 and closes only on `END` as the first piece of a body statement. Where it is stricter than `main`, PostgreSQL raises a syntax error.
    - The PR's 13-row case table splits as specified. 10 of 10 mutants of the new logic are killed by the PR's own rows.
    - Of the 532 tracked `.sql` files, 525 split as on `main`; the other 7 differ by design.
    - The shadow rendering of the real bootstrap lane is byte-identical to `main`'s, and it keeps the `91` statement. `lintRepository` gives 0 findings.
    - No new dependency, secret or injection surface. Gitleaks and Semgrep are green.
- **PR66-SEC-01 (LOW, CWE-436/CWE-693):** `tokenize` (unchanged by the PR) differs from `scan.l` in three ways:
  - (a) a lone CR ends a `--` comment;
  - (b) `é$a$` is an identifier, not a dollar quote;
  - (c) `$é$` is a dollar tag.

  Shapes (a) and (b) hide a `GRANT … TO platform_app` that PostgreSQL runs: the linter at the head gives 0 findings, against rule 8 for the control. Shape (c) fakes a `RESET ROLE` or an ENABLE + FORCE: rules 15 and 9 go silent.
  - **Who sees the raw text.** `migrate deploy` passes it to PostgreSQL with comments kept: Prisma 7.10.1's engine sends `sqlparser` pieces, or the whole script, through `simple_query`. The bootstrap runner does the same. The shadow rendering drops the comment, so it diverges from the real lane.
  - **Relation to the code review.** This is code review R1-m1, widened. One correction: the bootstrap runner keeps comments; it is the shadow rendering that drops them.
  - **Exposure.** None of the three shapes occurs in the 532 files or in PR #65's migration.
  - **Fix**, validated (all 532 token streams unchanged):
    - a CR also ends `--`;
    - use `isIdentifierChar` in the dollar rule;
    - accept a non-ASCII dollar-tag alphabet;
    - use the ASCII white-space class (R1-n1);
    - optionally, refuse a lone CR.
  - **Due:** this PR's fix cycle if one runs. Otherwise a `tools/db` follow-up (database-engineer), due before the next PR after #65 that adds or changes a migration or bootstrap file, and with any earlier change to `sql-text.ts`.
- **PR66-SEC-02 (INFO, CWE-693):** "never runs as a migration step" holds for utility statements (0A000) only. DML in a body runs when the routine is called, and rule 10 does not see a routine created and called in the same file (probe: 0 findings).
  - The wording goes to principal-architect at the next §8.3 edit.
  - The call-site rule, or a stated limit next to rule 11's PR #24 R1-n7, goes to the next holder of the `tools/db` linter.
- **Merge conditions (security):**
  1. The record is visible to ci-gate. It is committed on main, so it counts from the next `pull_request` event. A records-only commit after `9a14659` keeps the binding.
     - Simulated with main's checker: S1 to S5 pass, and C0 to C5 fail as expected.
     - C2 first hit a `git` timeout under host load; re-run alone, it gave the expected refusal.
  2. GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf is triaged repo-wide (no patched version is listed). Then a lane-A run must execute every fast-lane step green, including lint, type-check, unit, build, check-evidence and the base-ref negative fixtures.
  3. The security-integration job, which is due once `record_ok` is true, runs and passes.
  4. Any change to one of the 27 owned paths after `9a14659` needs a delta round.
- **Reversibility:** High.

### D-SECPR287B-01 · 2026-11-19 · security-analyst · TASK-287 part 287-B (workflow PR, branch `ci/TASK-287B-workflow`, not yet pushed) security round 1 = PASS_WITH_FOLLOW-UPS at code head `06f62ac` (record `docs/05-quality/security/PR-pending-TASK-287B-security-review.md`, committed on main; to be renamed `PR-<NNNN>-TASK-287B-security-review.md` once the PR exists)
- **Decision:** 0 Critical, High, Medium or Low; 2 INFO (PR287B-SEC-01, PR287B-SEC-02), both pre-existing defence in depth routed to 287-C. The record binds to the code commit `06f62ac` through its single `Head` row. The evidence-only tip changes no owned path, so main's checker accepts it through the merge ref. Simulation: 11 of 11 scenarios as expected, 4 passing and 7 controls failing. The controls cover the placeholder name, no record, a later FAIL row, a wrong `Head`, an owned or `ci.yml` change after the head, and another PR number. Host rule: static review plus single-process Node probes on `git archive` extracts. Three read-only git commands ran in the PR worktree at the start; this is disclosed in the record.
- **Closed:**
  - **PR62-SEC-02.** The policy accepts V2 only, and the four `FAST_LANE_*` aggregation entries are required with their exact values. The transitional `pinnedScriptAlternativesProblems` and `envOptional` are deleted. The merge-base and head policies ran over 1,229 mutants of the head `ci.yml`: 0 are weaker at the head, and the 10 stricter ones are exactly the designed ones.
  - **PR59-SEC-01 item 2, workflow half.** Both tooling steps check `HEAD == GITHUB_SHA` before the tested-base lines. In real bash, a crafted merge with an attacker's first parent fails closed under V2 and writes nothing to `$GITHUB_ENV`; under V1 (the control) it becomes `TOOLS_REF`. `GITHUB_*` names are refused at every env level. With item 1 (287-A), PR59-SEC-01 is closed once this merges.
  - **PR55-SEC-05, workflow half.** The aggregation now receives the four outputs. Main's gate already reports `fast-lane outputs mismatch` on any difference, so the compare is live from this PR's own run.

A full run only adds gates. Code review R1-m1 (MINOR) and R1-n1 of this round are minutes and UX items, not security findings. If R1-m1 is fixed in this cycle it must only add conjuncts, and it needs a delta security round.
- **D-SEC-PR62-01 interim rule kept:** no `uses:` commit changed and no action step gained `env:` in any workflow. The only step-env change is the four entries on the aggregation `run:` step. Permissions, triggers, job env and token placement are unchanged. No `${{ }}` appears in any `run:`.

  - **PR287B-SEC-01 (INFO, CWE-693, A08:2021).** `lane-scope.mjs` `gateInputStage2FromEnv` still skips an absent `FAST_LANE_*` entry, so the requirement lives only in the policy. Fix in 287-C: absence gives `fast-lane outputs missing (<keys>)`, with a test row. Owner: devops-engineer.
  - **PR287B-SEC-02 (INFO, CWE-693, A08:2021).** The stage-2 job shape is a deny-list. `runs-on` (including `self-hosted`) and `environment` are accepted on fast-lane, security-integration and ci-gate under both policies. This fails closed today because no self-hosted runner exists. Fix in 287-C, with PR62-SEC-01: an exact job key set and `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04`. Owner: devops-engineer.

### D-ARCH-154 · 2026-11-19 · principal-architect · PR #65 R1-m1 (b): references between organisation-keyed tables are composite foreign keys through `org_id`, in the TASK-037 migration now; rule T1/T2 and catalog assertion C16 for every later table (ADR-0005 amendment 13 items 27 and 28)
- **Decision:**
  - In `20261117000000_organisations_identity`, before it merges: `membership_roles (org_id, membership_id) → memberships (org_id, id)` and `memberships (org_id, invitation_id) → invitations (org_id, id)` replace the two single-column keys and keep their names. `memberships` and `invitations` each gain a unique index `ux_<table>__org_id_id` on `(org_id, id)`.
  - The service fix of R1-m1 (a) stays. The key is the control for the case where the service is wrong.
  - Rule for every later table (data-model §4.7). T1: a reference from a table with `org_id NOT NULL` to another table that carries `org_id` is composite through `org_id`. T2: where `org_id` is nullable on the referencing side (GUEST_CAPABLE), the single-column key stays and the composite key is added beside it.
  - Catalog assertion C16 (data-model §4.6) checks the rule, with an exception map that starts empty. Default owner TASK-293, fallback TASK-051. Due before the next migration that adds such a reference merges.
  - Outside the rule: references to GLOBAL tables, to `organisations` and to `users`, and the logical actor columns.
- **Why:**
  - PostgreSQL runs referential-integrity checks without row security. Probed on the PR's migration: in the context of organisation A, a role row with `org_id = A` naming B's membership is accepted. B's own grant of that role to that member then fails with `23505` while B sees no role row. A can block a role grant in B, and the key and the index answer questions about B's data.
  - RLS `WITH CHECK` cannot help, because the forged row carries A's own `org_id`.
  - Now is the cheapest point: the tables are empty and the file is mutable. After the merge it is an expand migration per table pair (concurrent unique index in its own file, `NOT VALID`, `VALIDATE`).
  - Cost: one unique index per referenced table (32-byte key, about 50 MB per million rows, estimated), one more index insertion per parent insert, nothing on the referencing table.
  - No policy, template, manifest or renderer rule changes, so the DR-A14 sign-off is not reopened.
- **Alternatives rejected:**
  - Service-layer checks only: leaves the table open to exactly the defect class RLS exists for (NFR-SEC-011).
  - A trigger that compares the parent's `org_id`: an invoker trigger cannot see the other tenant's row, a definer one adds a privileged read, and each reference needs its own.
  - Later, in an expand migration: three files per table pair, and every table added meanwhile repeats the finding.
- **Verified here:** single-process PGlite 17.5 probes on a patched scratch copy of the developer's migration, with the unpatched file as the negative control (cross-tenant reference `23503`, own reference ok, registration shape ok, the six generated-suite probe shapes unchanged against committed seed rows with dangling references, C16 sketch 0 rows against 2 unpatched). `prisma validate` and `prisma migrate diff --from-empty` accept the schema form and emit the same four statements. `tools/db/lint-migrations.ts` reports no findings on the patched file. Rule T2 was checked on a two-table probe only.
- **Not verified here:** no Jest, type check or container run. PGlite is PostgreSQL 17. Lane B on the fix head is the evidence. The index cost is an estimate.
- **Open:** binding guest rows of GUEST_CAPABLE tables through `guest_token_hash`. Ruled with database-engineer before TASK-051 writes the quotes migration (risks.md R-ARCH-34).
- **Where:** `docs/03-architecture/rulings/wave-1-pr65-r1-rulings.md` §2 and §5 (exact statements, Prisma form, tests); ADR-0005 amendment 13 items 27 and 28; data-model §1.1 P12, §3.2, §4.6 C16, §4.7, A31; risks.md R-ARCH-34.
- **Reversibility:** High until PR #65 merges. After that, dropping a composite key is a contract migration; the rule itself can be relaxed per table through the C16 exception map.

### D-ARCH-155 · 2026-11-19 · principal-architect · PR #65 R1-n1: an invitation row exists only in a `BUSINESS_CUSTOMER` organisation; the trigger is made stricter and the data-model stands (ADR-0005 amendment 13 item 30)
- **Decision:**
  - `platform.role_scope_matches_org()` gains one check for the `invitations` table: the organisation's type is `BUSINESS_CUSTOMER`. With the existing scope mapping the invited role is then always a customer role.
  - The function stays shared and takes no argument. Both triggers and the marker `ROLE_NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_ORG_TYPE` are unchanged, so `ROLE_SCOPE_GUARDS` and its text pin in the generated suite do not move.
  - `membership_roles` is unaffected: operator roles in the operator organisation and the Owner link of a personal organisation still pass.
  - The service answers first (TASK-227: 422 `ORG_TYPE_RESTRICTION` or `ROLE_NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_ORG_TYPE`). The trigger is the backstop.
- **Why:**
  - REQ-ORG-010 invites into a `BUSINESS_CUSTOMER` organisation. REQ-ACCT-014 and A-082 exclude INDIVIDUAL organisations, and DR-A05 gives them exactly one member.
  - `OPERATOR_SUPER_ADMIN` holds every role-assignable permission, `org:member:invite` included, with the operator organisation as its active organisation. Once the invitation route exists, the looser trigger admits an invitation for an operator role. Whoever accepts it becomes operator staff with cross-tenant read, outside the staff controls of M2 (EPIC-B-207) and the first-staff command of D-ARCH-153.
  - Probed: on the unpatched file the operator-role invitation in the operator organisation and a customer-role invitation in a personal organisation are both accepted; with the check both raise `P0001`.
- **Alternatives rejected:**
  - Reword the data-model to the looser mapping: it would document a privilege path that no requirement asks for.
  - A second trigger function, or a trigger argument: more objects or a changed text pin for the same effect.
  - Leave it to TASK-227: the migration is immutable after the merge, and a later fix is a second migration for a rule that is known today.
- **Later:** staff or partner onboarding by invitation (M2, M3) replaces the function in a new migration under an ADR-0005 amendment.
- **Where:** rulings file §3 and §5.2 item 4; ADR-0005 amendment 13 item 30; data-model §3.2 `invitations`, `membership_roles`.
- **Reversibility:** High (a function body; `CREATE OR REPLACE` by its owner in a later migration).

### D-ARCH-156 · 2026-11-19 · principal-architect · PR #65 security flag S1: a database control is required in this migration, the `AFTER ROW` trigger `trg_memberships__lifecycle_guard`; the service rule alone does not stand (ADR-0005 amendment 13 item 29)
- **Decision:**
  - `memberships` carries an assertion trigger (`AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF user_id, org_id, status`, function `platform.memberships_lifecycle_guard()`, `SECURITY INVOKER`, fixed search path) that raises `P0001 MEMBERSHIP_LIFECYCLE_VIOLATION` unless:
    1. on insert, `user_id = platform.app_actor_id()`;
    2. on insert, `status = 'ACTIVE'`;
    3. on update, `user_id` and `org_id` are unchanged;
    4. on update, a `REMOVED` row keeps that status.
  - No exemption for the SYSTEM actor or for any role.
  - Provisioning code (demo seed, staff-provisioning function of TASK-089, `ops:staff-bootstrap` at M5) runs the membership insert with the member as `app.actor_id`, as it already must for the `users` insert. The audit actor type and run reference are fields of the audit entry, not `app.actor_id`.
  - Default from now on: a new assertion trigger on an RLS table is `AFTER ROW` unless it has a stated reason to run earlier. The standard-columns guard, the de-claim guard and the two role-scope triggers stay `BEFORE`.
- **Why:**
  - `p_memberships__tenant` lets any session of an organisation write a membership row, and `p_users__org_member_read` shows the user of an ACTIVE or SUSPENDED membership to that organisation. Probed on the unpatched file: actor A in context A inserts an ACTIVE membership for user B and then reads B's `users` row.
  - D-ARCH-123 removed `INVITED` from the policy list for this reason. The reason holds for ACTIVE as well; that ruling closed the design path and left the table open.
  - In all three creating paths (registration, organisation creation, invitation acceptance) the new member is already the actor, so the rule costs the product nothing. DR-A05 and REQ-ORG-003 already state rules 2 to 4.
  - It ships in this migration, although a trigger could be added later, because the security sign-off on `p_users__org_member_read` rests on who can create a membership, and because TASK-049, 089, 224, 227 and 231 all build fixtures on this table.
  - `AFTER ROW` keeps RLS `WITH CHECK` first: a cross-tenant write still fails as `42501`, the generated suite keeps proving `WITH CHECK` on `memberships` without a new trait, and C15 (b) is not in play.
- **Alternatives rejected:**
  - Insert only through a definer function with `INSERT` revoked: a write-capable definer function and a write policy for `platform_definer`, against ADR-0005 amendments 6 and 12 item 25. It would test the same condition and would not cover updates.
  - A restrictive `FOR INSERT` policy: a new policy kind in the DR-A14 memberships template (renderer allow-list, rule 9, C3, the §4.3 fence, the sign-off), and a policy cannot compare OLD and NEW.
  - Require an accepted invitation: invitations are tenant-writable too, and two of the three creating paths have none.
  - An exemption for the SYSTEM actor: it reopens the hole for every job context.
  - Service rule with a tracked task: leaves the table open in the migration whose policies are being signed off.
- **Verified here:** PGlite probes as in D-ARCH-154: the foreign-user insert is refused and the user's row stays invisible (unpatched: accepted, 1 row); own ACTIVE insert ok and visible to a fellow member; non-ACTIVE at creation, `user_id` change and leaving `REMOVED` refused; `ACTIVE ↔ SUSPENDED → REMOVED` ok; re-parenting refused by RLS as `platform_app` and by the guard as the superuser in origin mode; the SEC-TC-74 forged-creator case still answers `STD_COLUMNS_VIOLATION`.
- **Consequence:** a path in which an organisation enrols a user who is not the actor (directory provisioning, staff management by an administrator) needs an ADR-0005 amendment and a migration that replaces the function.
- **Where:** rulings file §4 and §5.2 item 5, §5.4; ADR-0005 amendment 13 item 29; data-model §1.7, §3.2 `memberships`, §4.3, §4.7, §9.1, §9.3.
- **Reversibility:** High (a trigger and a function; replaceable in a later migration without touching data).

### D-ARCH-157 · 2026-11-19 · principal-architect · Invitation acceptance: the membership's `created_by` is the accepting user; "`created_by` = the inviter" of D-ARCH-123 / D-067 is withdrawn (wording routed to product-manager)
- **Decision:** at `POST /invitations/accept` the membership is inserted with `created_by` = the accepting user, who is the actor of the transaction. The inviter is `invitations.created_by`, reached through `memberships.invitation_id`, which D-ARCH-154 binds to the same organisation.
- **Why:** `platform.std_columns_guard()` (D-ARCH-091, shipped by PR #65) refuses an insert whose `created_by` is not the transaction's actor. D-ARCH-123 was written after that guard and contradicts it. Running the acceptance as the inviter would misstate who acted and would fail rule 1 of D-ARCH-156. ### D-ARCH-158 · 2026-11-19 · principal-architect · Re-specification (CLAUDE.md §7 rung 2) of the TASK-291 web prerender item: split out as late task TASK-294 `flake3f` (TASK-W0-FLAKE-3-F; test-engineer, M, opus, batch 7.9, due before G3), interim re-run rule in `docs/07-ops/CI-CD.md` §1 (ADR-0023 amendment O), TASK-291 narrowed to what was built; plan regenerated: 294 tasks, 82 batches, 0 errors, 0 warnings
- **Trigger:** code review r1 of TASK-291 (`docs/05-quality/reviews/PR-pending-TASK-291-code-review.md`, R1-M1; merge conditions C1, C2, C4). The developer applied the card's fallback, the procedural rule (D-TASK291-04), without the 20-build measurement that the fallback depends on. The review offered a re-scope record as option (b); this entry is that record. It is rung 2, not rung 3: TASK-291 is a story-less enabler, so no Must is deferred or split and product-manager is not involved. No fix cycle is counted for this item.
- **Root cause (the card, D-ARCH-146, not the developer):**
  1. **The method could not be run.** The card asked for "a reproduction under the PR #53 load method". I found no load generator behind those words. The 20-run tables of PR #53 and PR #57 were taken on the host as it then was, saturated by parallel heavy runs (D-ORCH-096/097; the PR #53 review says "on the saturated host"). D-ORCH-125, on the day the card was written, ended that state: lane B is a serial queue with no Testcontainers container and at least 7 GB free before a run, and agents no longer start `quality:heavy`. D-ORCH-130 shows what recreating it costs (the low-memory reaper). A developer agent could not take the measurement inside these rules.
  2. **Wrong bundling.** A measurement that needs the shared host on its own was a merge-blocking line of a code task that holds four locks, `api-routing` and `tests-gen-rls` among them.
  3. **A fallback with no reachable precondition.** The procedural rule was allowed only "when the measurement warrants neither form of (2)". The card had no branch for "the measurement cannot be taken now".
  4. **An undecidable target.** "The lightest control that brings the lane B build under 1 %" cannot be shown by 20 builds: no failure in 20 still leaves a 95 % upper bound near 14 %.
  5. **One wrong fact in the phase list.** The card named "preview-server start" as a candidate slow phase. In `@react-router/dev` 8.5.1 the preview server is awaited before any request is issued, so its start is outside the 10 s window. What the window covers is the first request: reaching the handler, the lazy import of the server bundle (cached for the later requests) and the render, in the one process that both serves and issues the request.
- **Decision:**
  1. **Split.** The prerender item leaves TASK-291 and becomes part 294-A of the new late task **TASK-294** `flake3f` (alias TASK-W0-FLAKE-3-F): test-engineer, M, opus, locks `quality-tools` and `tests-harness`, depends on TASK-291, in the free slot of batch 7.9, so it is due before the G3-ready checkpoint and holds neither the Wave 0 nor the Wave 1 exit. Part 294-A is a measurement with a record and a decision, delivered as a docs-only PR; it needs no lock. It runs as one dedicated job of the serial lane B queue on an otherwise idle host, under a bounded synthetic load (CPU-bound children, one per logical core, plus one file-churn child; no second heavy run; free memory stays at or above 7 GB), with 20 idle and 20 loaded builds of the unmodified `@platform/web` build script.
  2. **A decidable outcome** (card line "294-A DECISION"). Row 1, application or configuration: the idle-host median first-request time is above 1 s, or the record shows an `apps/web` change that removes the failures; reported to the orchestrator for an `apps/web` task. Row 2, runner retry: otherwise, at least 2 of the 20 loaded builds fail or the interim rule has tripped (either contradicts a 1 % rate at about the 2 % level); the bounded retry of D-ARCH-146 in `tools/quality/heavy.mjs`, built in part 294-B. Row 3: otherwise no code, and the re-run rule becomes a standing operator rule.
  3. **Interim control.** Until 294-A closes, the rule "an `INVALID` lane B run with the prerender request-timeout signature is re-run once and is not a fix cycle" applies as an operator rule. Its single copy is `docs/07-ops/CI-CD.md` §1 "Lane B on the shared host: the serial queue and the prerender re-run rule (interim)", added in this commit; ADR-0023 amendment O carries the decision and the invariant. Compared with the card's sentence it adds: the exact signature and where it is read (the run log, not `summary.md`); the first attempt is moved aside and never committed; each use is recorded; one re-run per commit; and a trip condition (a failed re-run, or the second use within 20 consecutive queue runs) that makes 294-A the next queue job. The product build stays one un-retried `react-router build` (D-ARCH-146, unchanged).
  4. **TASK-291 narrowed to what was built.** Title without the prerender item; lock `quality-tools` released (no `tools/quality` file in scope); the files list names the three ratchet files and the `.github/CODEOWNERS` lines instead of `heavy.mjs`; the prerender line becomes a NOT HERE line. D-TASK291-04 does not stand as a card outcome. The proof at merge is the lane B run of the final head (review condition C2). **Routing asked for by C2:** the 20/20-under-load table of the converted suites and of the lock change is attached to the PR body when it was taken at that head; otherwise TASK-294 part 294-A owes it on the merged suites, with the Testcontainers start-failure rate of D-TASK288-15. The same root cause 1 applies to that table.
  5. **Nothing routed to W0-FLAKE-3 is dropped.** Five items that DECISIONS routed to TASK-291 after its card was written were not built and were not in the review's closure table: the two lane B runner items of D-ORCH-127 (pre-flight refusal of untracked run directories; inventory references tracked runs only), PR #57 code review R3-n1, R3-n2 and R3-n3 (D-ORCH-124), and the prisma-engines restore of D-TASK288-20. They are part 294-B, a code PR of its own that does not wait for 294-A. This goes one step beyond the brief for this ruling, which named only the prerender item; it is why the task is M and test-engineer, and the orchestrator can strike the line.
  6. **Plan.** `plan-data.mjs` and the regenerated `task-map.csv`, `WAVE-00.md`, `WAVE-07.md`: 294 tasks, 82 batches, 0 errors, 0 warnings. CSV diff: the TASK-291 row (title, refs) and one new row, TASK-294. IDs, waves, batches and branches of TASK-001..293 are unchanged (`feat/TASK-291-task-w0-flake-3-one` included). `PLAN.md` §3 count note updated.
- **Facts checked for this ruling:** the plugin source at 8.5.1 (timeout 10 s, `retryCount` 0, `concurrency` default 1, preview server awaited first, lazy cached server-bundle import). By that source the failing line reads `Prerender: Request failed for /en/: The operation was aborted due to timeout`; the plugin's "Request timed out for" wording needs an aborted request signal, which this version never sets. No failing log was kept, so the wording is not confirmed against a real failure: the CI-CD.md signature accepts both forms and the first use quotes the real line. The orchestrator's queue log kept since 2026-11-18 has 16 completed runs, no `INVALID` and no retry; this is an observation, not a rate.
- **Owed by others:**
  - **sdlc-orchestrator:** (a) the queue script re-runs today on any `INVALID` whose `summary.md` says "build failed or timed out"; narrow it to the signature in the run log, and record each use as CI-CD.md §1 item 3 says; (b) record D-TASK291-01..05 with 04 as "not accepted, replaced by D-ARCH-158"; (c) STATUS rows for TASK-291 and TASK-294 (parts 294-A and 294-B); (d) the delta review of this record by code-reviewer (condition C1).
  - **TASK-291 developer:** no document edit. The PR body says that the prerender item is not delivered and is TASK-294 (condition C4), and attaches the under-load table only if it was taken at the PR head.
  - **devops-engineer:** confirms the new CI-CD.md section at its next change of that file (the document is theirs; precedent D-ARCH-098 for TEST-STRATEGY).
- **Why:** the code of TASK-291 is sound and removes the pooled-socket flake class from the O3 runner suites, so holding it and its locks for an idle-host measurement costs more than it protects. The follow-up keeps the open question owned: whether "re-run once" hides an application-side regression. The trip condition bounds the interim rule in the meantime.
- **Alternatives rejected:**
  - **Queue the 20-build measurement now and hold TASK-291** (review option (a)): the method was not runnable as written (root cause 1), and the task's locks stay held for an idle-host window.
  - **Accept D-TASK291-04 as delivered:** a developer cannot waive a card deliverable, and nobody would own the open question.
  - **Build the `heavy.mjs` retry now, without measuring:** code in a security-owned runner for an event that the serial-queue log does not show; D-ARCH-146 says measure first.
  - **A retry or wrapper around the product build, or a patched timeout:** refused by D-ARCH-146; it would hide a real prerender regression in the images and the hosted build.
  - **The follow-up in batch 0.13, a new 0.14, or Wave 1:** a wave exit would wait for an idle-host job.
  - **A pure S measurement task for performance-engineer** (the orchestrator's default allowed it): the task also carries the under-load suite tables and the runner and test-lock leftovers, which are test-engineer work; a second card for five small items costs another PR and its CI minutes.
  - **Reproducing the load by running heavy lanes side by side:** against D-ORCH-125, and D-ORCH-130 shows the cost.
- **Reversibility:** High (plan data, one operator section, one ADR amendment). Part 294-A replaces the interim rule with its outcome.
